questions.question: What is the primary advantage of a linked list over an array?

options.text: Constant time for accessing elements by index
Dynamic size adjustment
Better cache locality
Faster searching

questions.question: What does each node in a singly linked list typically contain?

options.text: Only a data field
Two pointers to other nodes
A data field and a pointer to the next node
A pointer to the head of the list

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting a new node at the beginning of a singly linked list?

options.text: O(n)
O(log n)
O(n log n)

questions.question: Which of the following is true about doubly linked lists?

options.text: Each node has a single pointer
Insertion at the tail is O(n)
Traversal is possible only in one direction
Each node has pointers to both the next and the previous nodes

questions.question: What happens when a node is deleted in a singly linked list?

options.text: The entire list is reorganized
The next pointer of the previous node is updated
A new head node is created
The last node is removed instead
